card.summary: No free tier and no trial is published; 'A first box' is USD 3/month for 50 GB, with a 7-day money-back guarantee and no setup fee.

free_tier.stated: No free tier and no trial is published; 'A first box' is USD 3/month for 50 GB, with a 7-day money-back guarantee and no setup fee.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: sold by total storage (50 / 100 / 250 / 600 GB); no single-file cap is published

retention.stated: for the life of the subscription; no inactivity deletion is stated

egress.terms: 'unlimited downloads' and 'No caps' and 'unlimited torrents' on every plan, on an 'up to 1 Gbps' uplink. The page says nothing about an upload or seeding allowance, and nothing about transfer protocol.
egress.free_allowance: downloads stated unlimited; upload allowance not stated

record.interface_detail: The site lists ruTorrent, Deluge, qBittorrent, Transmission, Plex, Jellyfin, Sonarr and Radarr as one-click apps but does not name SFTP, FTP, rsync or any other retrieval path anywhere on the home or features page read.
record.tooling: Web panel with one-click apps; retrieval client is not documented, so it must be established in the client area before relying on it
record.chaining: A USD 3 box that is the cheapest per-month live offer after YourSeedbox; without a published retrieval protocol it is only usable once SFTP is confirmed at signup

limits.value: up to 1 Gbit/s shared, claimed identical on every tier

record.limits_note: No byte quota, no object cap and no published protocol: the honest reading is that the 50 GB disk is the binding practical limit and the retrieval method is unknown.
record.binding_note: Nothing in the vocabulary fails at 1 TiB/month on the published terms; the 50 GB disk forces roughly 21 cycles and the unstated retrieval protocol is the real risk.

identity_cost.detail: Account plus payment; no free tier. No phone or document check is stated.

record.reliability_note: Unlimited download and unlimited torrents are claims with no published fair-use threshold; the missing retrieval protocol is a support question before purchase, not a defect after it.
record.confidence_note: Prices, port speed, app list and refund window are on the live pages read. Two things keep this below measured: no transfer protocol is published and no slot was bought.

evidence.proved: Basic USD 3/mo 50 GB, Standard USD 5/mo 100 GB, Advance USD 8/mo 250 GB, Pro USD 15/mo 600 GB; 'Up to 1 Gbps'; 'unlimited downloads'; 'no setup fee'; 7-day money-back
one-click ruTorrent, Deluge, qBittorrent, Transmission, Plex, Jellyfin, Sonarr, Radarr; no retrieval protocol named

record.notes: The $3 tier answers 'under USD 5' on price but stores only 50 GB. Sustained-rate conversion: unlimited downloads claimed, so the comparable number is the 1 Gbit/s port, 125 MB/s; 1 TiB/month needs only 3.39 Mbit/s. Potential constraints: a hidden upload cap, an unstated protocol, or oversubscription; the first two are unstated on the page and the third is not observable without an account. cheapseedboxes.com states that EvoSeedbox and Iseedfast are its own seedbox services; they are documented as separate brands because they have separate sites, prices and plan structures.

extras.apps: ruTorrent, Deluge, qBittorrent, Transmission, Plex, Jellyfin, Sonarr, Radarr, one-click
